Sim Tiger

By: Busisiwe Gumede | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
11 year old golfer Simthandile Tshabalala is living his dream, jetting around the world and shining in local and international tournaments. He opens up about what motivates him and takes us on a journ

Unique Selling Point:
In just under three years of playing competitive golf, eight-year-old Simthandile
Tshabalala has made his mark on the sport, representing South Africa internationally
and winning a plethora of trophies. Tshabalala, who learned the game from YouTube
videos and has only been professionally coached for the last few years, has already
played at the Australian Open, where he came fourth, has played in Malaysia and
Scotland, and won the local US Kids Tour last year. He has also showcased his talent in
the United States, England and Canada. Fondly known as ‘Sim Tiger’, Tshabalala has
grabbed the attention of notable sponsors like TaylorMade, but the rest of his
increasingly expensive career is being funded by his father. Tshabalala
emerged victorious in the Junior Africa 2021 Challenge. This story will look into
Tshabalala’s career and bumpy road to success, the relationship he shares with his caddy (who also happens to be his father) and we probe efforts to make the sport more diverse, which many say aren't enough. What more needs to be done to make it more accessible to kids like Sims?

Summary:
Not many 11 year olds can brag about playing golf with President Cyril Ramaphosa. But golf prodigy Simthandile Tshabalala did that and more. He has well over 20 trophies and came second in his age group in the Australian Open 2020 in January. In November 2019 he was presented with the Sports Minister’s Excellence Award at the SA Sport Awards. He says he wants to be the best like Tiger Woods. Like his idol, he started playing golf at the age of four and quickly rose to stardom when he went professional in 2018.

It’s only been a year since he’s gained a professional coach and a sponsor – manufacturer, TaylorMade. Otherwise it is his father, Bonginkosi Tshabalala, who has been funding his career, making sure his son reaches his full potential. For father and son it’s been an incredible journey, spending lots of quality time together… something which Sim's father never had.

His father says he grew up with an absent father, with no male guidance or exposure to many things, so it’s very important that he provides this platform for his son. The only thing that he cannot get over, is his own son beating him at the game of golf.

in addition to his achievements, Sims also gives back to the community. He was recently been named the official Global Honorary Youth Ambassador for 67 Blankets for Nelson Mandela Day.

Press Release:


It began as a little boy's curious fascination with videos he found on YouTube.
But three-year-old Simthandile Tshabalala wasn’t interested in cartoons or anime,
he was spending his playtime, obsessively watching golf. By four years old, his father, Bonginkosi took
action to help his son develop this interestfor the game.
It soon became clear that Sim had amgolf swing that was far beyond his years.
Now 11-years-old, the golf prodigy has won multiple trophies. In 2020, he came second
in his age group at the prestigious Australian Open. Now he has set his sights
set on following in the footsteps of his idol, Tiger Woods, to master
the eighteen holes.

Producer:
Busisiwe Gumede-Chizhanje
| Presenter: Xola Ntshinga

Script:


VO - Golfers face many challenges: - wind, sand traps, water and - sometimes - their own uncertainties.

That’s why it’s surprising to find a young prodigy not yet in his teens, taking it all in his stride.

visuals - Sim places ball on ground, lifts head and adjusts his body to make a shot, and then swings.
BREATHER – natsound from golf viz
VO - 11-year-old Simthandile Tshabalala has a swing most adult golfers would trade their most prized clubs for. And he’s a bit of a charmer, too.

But, underneath it all, is an ambition to make it to the very top of this ultra competitive sport.



SIMTHANDILE TSHABALALA – GOLF CHAMPION

13:43 – 13:59 - ... Golf is, it's passionate to me. I love it. But to me, actually, golf really is, it's fun. …
VO – Simthandile first caught the eye of sports BROADCASTER, Robert Marawa, in 2020 when he was just 8 years old.
UPSOUND – Simthandile in studio on Robert's show - “And when I started playing it took me very fast to get better”.
ROBERT MARAWA – SPORT BROADCASTER


02:34 – 02:36 - ... you could tell that this kid is destined for success.
VO – It’s been just three years since that interview, and Simthandile has amassed more than 50 trophies from local and international tournaments. It’s earned him the nickname Sim Tiger, after arguably, the sport’s greatest of all time.


Visuals - Lets see tiger woods - hits ball, crowd stunned and celebrates..
ROBERT MARAWA – SPORT BROADCASTER


05:50 – 06:00 - ... We shouldn't be saying he's an elite athlete at the age of 11, but those are the qualities that he showed to us.
VO – And much like TIger Woods who rose to prominence with his father at his side, Simthandile's dad, Bonginkosi Tshabalala, is ever-present.




VO – Simthandile now has a professional coach, but it was a job held by Bonginkosi until a year ago. In fact, he was much more than that: before sponsors started showing interest, it fell to dad to cover the cost of training, international travel, accommodation and - yes - some of sport’s most expensive gear.


BONGINKOSI TSHABALALA – SIMTHANDILE'S FATHER

BONGINKOSI - - I wanted to give him that platform, which I did not have when I was young. When I was growing up, I didn't know anything about golf.

PRESENTER - Which is very fascinating because your life now, besides your professional career and obviously being a family man, you're also a caddy.

BONGINKOSI – Caddy daddy.

PRESENTER - Caddy daddy? It must be an interesting adaptation for you.

BONGINKOSI – So we used to not find each other from from when we were starting. I did not understand a few things about him. And then later on, he had to learn that within the course he's the boss. When off the course, I'm the boss.
VO – In the cut-and-thrust of competitive sport - even at this age - success demands absolute dedication…
BREATHER – viz of Simthandile in golf training with his dad, with a bit of natsound
SIMTHANDILE TSHABALALA – GOLF CHAMPION

PRESENTER - 05:43 – 05:49 - ... You stay excited about golf, but you play so much of it. How many hours do you put in a day?

SIMTHANDILE - 05:50 – 06:00 - ... I'll go to my coach for an hour in the morning, so estimated two or 3 hours a day.

PRESENTER - So what time do you get up?

SIMTHANDILE – Well, half past four.

PRESENTER – 06:04 - Every day. Monday to Friday?

SIMTHANDILE – Monday to Friday. 06:09 – 06:25 - ... Got to work hard. And also, there's also training, I’ve got to keep fit. And I also need to eat healthy.
VO –Throw in the need to stay on top of schoolwork, and it’s a workload most adults would struggle with. But, the sacrifice is paying off: Simthandile is now a three-time U.S. Kids Tour Champion, 2020 Australian Open runner-up and is 7th in the world of kids’ golf rankings.

visuals - Simthandile going through his trophies..
SIMTHANDILE TSHABALALA – GOLF CHAMPION

16:39 – 16:52 - When I see all my trophies, I feel like, wow, you've actually done this.
BREATHER – viz of president's Golf Day with a bit of upsound, carry visuals over the next VO
VO – Then in 2020, and just 9-years-old, Simthandile got a call from Cyril Ramaphosa's office and an invite to play in the President’s annual Golf Day.
SIMTHANDILE TSHABALALA – GOLF CHAMPION

11:45 – 11:56 - ... I would stand behind the ball. I'll check my line to the wind. Check with a danger is especially that's a big part of the game. 11:57 - This is called course management.


VO – And, it seems, that’s a lesson the President has yet to learn: with cameras rolling, Simthandile showed the first citizen flames - as his generation would say.


BREATHER – continue with above, carry the visuals into the next upsound where Robert says “beautiful moment, beautiful touch from the president.
ROBERT MARAWA – SPORT BROADCASTER


03:25 – 03:31 - ... Beautiful moment, beautiful touch from the President. 03:32 - But is it enough? Is it enough just for the PR? 03:42 - ... it's also imperative for the very same President to take sports seriously, to make sure that his Department of Sports Arts and Culture take sports seriously. And outside of the PR, make sure that those elite young athletes like a Sim Tiger, are well looked after.
VO - Photo opps are one thing, ensuring our country’s children aren’ t denied opportunities in sport is quite another. while the department runs several - many would say underfunded-programs, none focus specifically on golf.

Sadly, that means other potential Simthandiles - especially those in townships lacking proper facilities - are being denied the chance to shine.
ROBERT MARAWA – SPORT BROADCASTER

04:18 – 04:22 - Imagine if Sim's dad was not a successful businessman as he is right now? It would be a different story. 04:23 - That would be a lost talent.
BREATHER – Simthandile playing
VO – As inspirational as Simthandile’s story is, he’s already endured his fair share of low points. He suffers from bouts of pain in his knee.
SIMTHANDILE TSHABALALA – GOLF CHAMPION

03:57 – 04:08 - It's getting better. Just did an X-ray today. One's waiting for results and it's just like it's been going around for maybe a year or so, but I believe it will get better.
VO – With injuries as much a part of sport as winning and losing, the show must go on..
SIMTHANDILE TSHABALALA – GOLF CHAMPION

16:00 – 16:06 - I think I'm doing an at least six tournaments in America. So I'm going to be there from, I think, June to August. 17:11 – 17:22 - I just really want to now want more trophies and I want to win the big tournaments. ... 17:34 – 17:44 - I call myself a pro junior or a junior pro, and I still have a long, long, long way to go. And I hope I really make it big in the future.
VO – There are no guarantees of success, not in a sport awash with child prodigies. But Simthandile stands as good a chance as any at following in his hero's footsteps.
